property_summary: For any interfaceId, the original C correctly returns true when given type(IERC1155).interfaceId while the mutant incorrectly returns false.

For any interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId exactly when supportsInterface in ERC165 returns true OR interfaceId matches type(IERC1155).interfaceId; the mutant returns false when interfaceId == type(IERC1155).interfaceId but base-supports do not also claim it, breaking ERC165 compliance.
For any valid interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true when interfaceId equals type(IERC1155).interfaceId, but the mutant incorrectly returns false for this case.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(id) must return true when id equals type(IERC1155).interfaceId, because the reference implementation ORs this check; the mutant removes it, returning false instead.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId; the bug incorrectly returns false for that identifier.

For any interfaceId that is neither type(IERC1155).interfaceId nor a super interface, supportsInterface must return false; the bug incorrectly returns true for type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId because it skips the IERC1155MetadataURI check but still falls through to super.supportsInterface which returns true for it.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId; the bug incorrectly returns false for type(IERC1155).interfaceId because it skips the explicit check and the super call does not handle it.

For any valid interfaceId, supportsInterface returns true if and only if the interfaceId matches IERC1155, IERC1155MetadataURI, or a supported super-interface; the buggy version incorrectly returns false for IERC1155MetadataURI.interfaceId.

For any interfaceId that is not explicitly handled in the override chain, the contract must inherit the result from its parent ERC165; the buggy version skips the valid IERC1155MetadataURI check but incorrectly passes it to super.supportsInterface, which returns true for it, while the correct version returns true because of the explicit check, but the bug manifests as a discrepancy for unsupported interfaces that happen to be handled by ERC165.

For any bytes4 input, the reference C.supportsInterface returns true if the interfaceId matches IERC1155, IERC1155MetadataURI, or the parent ERC165, while the buggy version requires all three conditions to be true simultaneously, so it returns false for inputs where only one or two match.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, the reference C's supportsInterface returns true if the interfaceId matches any of IERC1155, IERC1155MetadataURI, or ERC165, but the buggy version requires all three to match, so it returns false for interfaceId that match only one or two.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when the id matches any of IERC1155, IERC1155MetadataURI, or ERC165; the mutant erroneously requires all three matches simultaneously, returning false for ids that only match one or two of them.

The reference C supports an interface if the ID matches any of IERC1155, IERC1155MetadataURI, or ERC165; the mutant requires all three matches, so it returns false when the ID matches exactly one or two of them.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when either ID equals IERC1155's ID, IERC1155MetadataURI's ID, or ERC165's ID (as inherited), and the buggy AND logic returns false for IDs that match only one or two of these.

For any non-zero address and valid token ID, the balanceOf function should return the actual balance minted to that account, not always zero; the buggy version always returns zero, breaking this invariant.

For any address that has ever been minted a positive amount of a token via _mint, the reference balanceOf returns a strictly positive value, while the mutant always returns zero, violating the invariant that minted balances are non-zero.

For any address and token ID where the address has a positive balance minted via `_mint`, the reference `balanceOf` returns the actual minted amount, while the mutant always returns 0, violating the rule that minted balances are reflected in `balanceOf`.

For any account and token ID, if a non-zero amount has been minted to that account, then balanceOf(account, id) should be strictly greater than zero in the reference, but the mutant always returns zero.

For any account and token ID where an allowance has been set for daily spending tracking, the getAllowanceRemaining view function must reflect the actual allowance state, but the mutant's broken balanceOf causes allowance logic to fail, violating the invariant that getAllowanceRemaining correctly reports remaining allowance.
